tectonic.notes: Zero-config offline binary bundled in repository. Auto-caches packages and OpenType fonts locally.

xelatex.notes: Local xelatex not installed on Windows host. Standard TeX Live server environment baseline metrics applied.

wasm.notes: Client-side WASM engine. Requires downloading ~40-50MB TeX bundle (binary + format + fonts). Heavy initial memory allocation (256MB-512MB heap). Sub-optimal for instant editing preview compared to server-side compile queue.

decisionSummary.primaryServer: XeLaTeX (via Docker TeX Live container in Spring Boot apps/api)
decisionSummary.offlineDev: Tectonic CLI (bundled directly in bin/tectonic.exe for local zero-config offline builds)
decisionSummary.browserWasm: Deferred to non-blocking future exploration (bundle size 40MB+ and heap overhead too high for core editor)
keyRationales: XeLaTeX is the gold standard for academic publisher class files (.cls), full fontspec OpenType and microtype support.
XeLaTeX has battle-tested sandbox security using the --no-shell-escape flag to prevent arbitrary code execution.
Tectonic provides blazing-fast local developer experience (warm compile ~1.0-1.2s) with zero external setup on Windows/Linux.
Tectonic supports --untrusted flag, preventing shell escapes and unsafe write operations.
In-browser WASM TeX engines require 40-50MB initial asset downloads and 256MB+ heap, which degrades user experience on average client machines.
